dedupe_keys.name: thermal comfort and urban heat island redesign of a public open space in rome envi met

description: This study examined how the urban heat island affects thermal comfort and the use of an urban open space in Rome, Italy, and sought a method that urban designers can follow to reduce heat island impacts and improve comfort outdoors. The authors argue that people use parks, squares, streets and foot and cycle paths more when those spaces are comfortable, and that urban form can mitigate the combined effect of climate change and the heat island. Microclimate and user thermal perception were assessed through PET, PMV and PPD values from ENVI-met simulations, and the Sustainable Development Goals served as design guidelines. Coverage: one public open space in Rome. Access: open-access article in Scientific Reports (2024). Licence: CC-BY-4.0 article. Caveats: a simulation-based design study of one site, without post-construction monitoring. Outcome: a masterplan redesign built on sustainable design principles to improve the site microclimate and comfort. Simulation uses: testing shading, vegetation and material options for squares and streets before redesign. Related records: ENVI-met, the ENVI-met Milan and Pescara microclimate data, and urbanMicroclimateFoam.

name: Thermal comfort and urban heat island redesign of a public open space in Rome (ENVI-met)
organisations: Nour M. Ahmed, Paola Altamura, Marco Giampaoletti, Fahd A. Hemeida and co-authors
outcomes: The study proposed a masterplan redesign of the Rome site based on sustainable design principles to improve its microclimate and users' thermal comfort, and set out a method urban designers can follow to reduce urban heat island effects in outdoor space.
